rules: GPU required; CPU fallback is forbidden. All fitting and clustering use torch on CUDA in float64.
The true partition is used only to generate tasks and evaluate the oracle and structural diagnostics.
A Ward hierarchy with a fixed zero group is extracted only from dense source least-squares solutions. It contains every K from 128 through zero; no true K is passed to extraction or selection.

K, PCA rank and dense ridge strength are selected on eight separate source-calibration tasks at the exact target support size. Target examples are generated only after all choices for that bank are frozen.
Targets from a bank share one unknown base partition. Residuals are independent across tasks, orthogonal to that partition, and have the declared norm.

The principal outcome is exact population prediction MSE against the noiseless teacher, equal to squared coefficient error under isotropic Gaussian inputs. Observed-label risk additionally includes noise variance.

Dense minimum-norm least squares is the converged zero-initialized GD reference. Dense and adaptive GD curves use 512 steps, zero initialization and a stable step based on the support design spectral norm.

Methods: dense min-norm, source-calibrated dense ridge, adaptive partition, base-partition oracle, source PCA with selected rank, random partition matched to adaptive group sizes, dense GD and adaptive GD.
Save support/query MSE curves and auxiliary positive-sign recall. Recall concerns sign classification and is not the main regression criterion.
Summarize independent source banks first. Task repetitions within a bank are not independent bank replications.

This is a mechanism pilot for statistical transfer and adaptive K, not a neural-network or autoregressive-generator benchmark. Report source fitting, hierarchy and calibration costs separately from target fitting. Do not add or run tests.
